title: Classes and objects check
instructions: Five questions on classes, objects and methods.

options: The particular object the method was called on
A reserved word that does nothing
questions.explanation: self is the object the method was called on. Python passes it automatically.

options: Only when you call it yourself
questions.explanation: Python calls __init__ automatically each time you create an object, so it sets up the starting data.

questions.prompt: After a = Account('Ada', 100), b = Account('Linus') and a.deposit(25), what is b.balance (the default balance is 0)?
questions.explanation: Each object keeps its own attributes. Changing a does not touch b.

questions.prompt: Inside a method, what does `balance += amount` (without self.) do when balance is an attribute?
questions.explanation: Without self. Python treats balance as a local variable that has no value yet. Attributes are reached through self.

questions.prompt: A function written inside a class is called a...
questions.explanation: Functions defined inside a class are methods. Data stored on an object is an attribute.

title: Build an Account class
instructions:
Write a class `Account`:

- `Account(owner, balance=0)` stores `owner` and `balance`.
- `deposit(amount)` adds to the balance.
- `withdraw(amount)` takes money out and returns `True`, but if the balance is too small it changes nothing and returns `False`.

There is nothing to print. Your class is tested directly.

tests.description: Account('Ada', 100) starts with a balance of 100
withdrawing 30 from 100 returns True and leaves 70
withdrawing 500 from 100 returns False and leaves 100
